intent: Quantify how lost tax revenue changes across the reported range of cheating rates.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
How does lost tax revenue change across the reported range of cheating rates?

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: Lost tax revenue increases monotonically from $44.7B at a 1 percentage-point increase in cheating to $185.7B at a 4 percentage-point increase, rising across the full reported range.
units.computation: Compare successive values: 44.7 < 90.5 < 137.5 < 185.7; total increase = 185.7 - 44.7 = 141.0 billion USD over x from 1 to 4.
accept: Lost tax revenue rises as the percentage-point increase in cheating rises from 1 to 4.
Values increase from 44.7 to 90.5 to 137.5 to 185.7 billion USD.
The overall change is an increase of 141.0 billion USD across the reported range.
reject: Lost tax revenue decreases as cheating increases.
The relationship is flat or non-monotonic across the reported range.
Only the endpoints are mentioned without indicating the upward trend across the range.

optional_valid: Mentioning the absolute difference between the first and last values (141.0 billion USD).
Mentioning the approximate ratio or percentage change from first to last value.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for why lost tax revenue increases.
Claims about values outside the reported x range of 1 to 4.
Claims about other panels or series not present in the table.
review_notes: Single-panel, single-series line chart; one trend unit captures the requested change across the reported range.
Endpoints, absolute difference, and ratio are treated as alternative evidence for the same trend slot and merged into U1.
